title.rendered: What is the difference between woven and knitted mesh?

acf.question: What is the difference between woven and knitted mesh?
acf.answer: Woven mesh provides controlled openings and stable geometry through interlaced wires, while knitted mesh uses looped wire construction for greater flexibility and conformability. The correct structure depends on flow, conductivity, strength and integration requirements.

title.rendered: What is the difference between Voltra Lite, Voltra + and Voltra Max?

acf.question: What is the difference between Voltra Lite, Voltra + and Voltra Max?
acf.answer:
Voltra Lite is low density, single wire per needle — used for open GDL and elastic elements.

Voltra + is medium density, double wire per needle — used as a separator.

Voltra Max is high density, three or more wires per needle — used for dense GDL and electrode support.

Wires per needle sets GDL density and conductivity; needle gauge and stitch length set pore size and stack-cell fit.

title.rendered: Which materials can BVK Hydrotech weave and knit?

acf.question: Which materials can BVK Hydrotech weave and knit?
acf.answer:
Common alloys including carbon steel and stainless steel (1.4301/304, 1.4306/304L, 1.4401/316, 1.4404/316L, 1.4841/314, 1.4539/904L), and modern alloys including Nickel and nickel-based alloys up to Ni 99.6, Crofer 22H (1.4760), Hastelloy C-22 (2.4602), Inconel 625 (2.4956), copper (2.0060), aluminium (3.3555) and titanium.

Material is selected against the performance criteria of the application, not from a fixed catalogue.
